headline: South Asia: ‘Calibrated’ air strikes target terrorist hideouts at two locations in Afghanistan: info ministry
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: ‘Calibrated’ air strikes target terrorist hideouts at two locations in Afghanistan: info ministry.
- Persian Gulf Region: Afghanistan says Pakistani airstrikes killed women and children.
- Western Russia: Ukrainian forces strike drone site and Russian arms depot, destroy Rubicon warehouses.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: Samuda warns tougher water curbs coming.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Samuda warns tougher water curbs coming.
Water Minister Matthew Samuda is warning that tougher water restrictions are coming as Jamaica continues to grapple with a crippling drought, signalling an escalation in the Government’s response to the prolonged dry spell. The minister gave the dire update during yesterday’s post-Cabinet press briefing at Jamaica House in St Andrew. The National Water Commission (NWC) imposed water prohibition orders on August 17, restricting the use of NWC-supplied water for non-essential activities such as watering lawns, washing vehicles and refilling pools across seven parishes.
United States - bottom line: Hegseth announces new four-star command for autonomous warfare.
- Military Times, 17 hours ago: Hegseth announces new four-star command for autonomous warfare.
The new Autonomous Warfare Command, or AutoWarCom, aims to address an acquisition system that isn't keeping pace with the speed of technological change.
- Military Times, 19 hours ago: 8 sailors died by suicide at Oklahoma base in one year, Navy confirms.
The deaths, along with eight attempted suicides in the USS Abraham Lincoln strike group, illustrate a systemic problem in the U.S. Navy, families say.
- Military Times, 19 hours ago: US Air Force awards $2.38B contract to Boeing for 22 F-15EX.
The service awarded Boeing a contract for 22 more F-15EX aircraft, bringing the number to a total of 120 to be manufactured by the defense company.
- Military Times, 23 hours ago: First elements of USS Abraham Lincoln strike group return home.
The first ship within the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group, the USS Frank E. Petersen Jr., has returned home after its 10-month-long deployment.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: ‘Calibrated’ air strikes target terrorist hideouts at two locations in Afghanistan: info ministry.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: ‘Calibrated’ air strikes target terrorist hideouts at two locations in Afghanistan: info ministry.
Pakistan carried out “well-planned and calibrated” air strikes against terrorist hideouts in Afghanistan, the information ministry said on Thursday. In a post on X, the ministry said the strikes were carried out in continuation of Operation Ghazab lil Haq and Pakistan’s resolve to eliminate terrorists, their networks and supporters. It said the aerial strikes targeted the hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations it referred to as Fitna al Khwarij and Fitna al Hindustan, and resulted in the deaths of “multiple terrorists”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: ‘Why the need for all this drama’: DG ISPR lampoons India's 'neutralised Pakistani terrorist' claims, presents him before media.
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry lampooned India’s claims of “neutralising” a “terrorist” allegedly linked to the Pakistani military, presenting the individual during a press conference on Thursday. The press conference comes after Indian media reported that an individual wanted in connection with the April 22 Pahalgam terrorist attack last year had been killed during an “encounter” in Indian Illegally Occupied Kashmir’s Korag area.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Guardian - Australia, Al Jazeera - Middle East, Jerusalem Post, The Hindu - International, Times of India - Top Stories, just now: UAE says investigation launched into diverted flydubai flight.
The United Arab Emirates’ chief prosecutor on Thursday ordered an investigation into the incident aboard flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, which made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after a reported altercation in the cockpit. The state news agency WAM said the attorney general had ordered the probe, adding that “the investigation team has launched its work into the incident” that forced the plane to land in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Security forces kill 6 terrorists in IBO in Balochistan's Kachhi: security sources.
Security forces killed six terrorists in an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Balochistan’s Kachhi district, security sources said on Thursday, according to state-run Radio Pakistan. According to security sources, terrorists affiliated with Fitna al Hindustan were successfully targeted using quadcopters in Kachhi’s Sanni area. The state refers to designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. Radio Pakistan reported that a large quantity of arms and ammunition was recovered from the terrorists.

India - bottom line: Flydubai hero pilot Smit Machchhar to be awarded ‘Visisht Gujarat Garima Award’.
- Times of India - Top Stories, NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Flydubai hero pilot Smit Machchhar to be awarded ‘Visisht Gujarat Garima Award’.
Captain Smit Machchhar was injured by his co-pilot who planned to crash their aircraft. Despite being attacked, Machhar managed to save the lives of 174 passengers. The courageous actions of Machhar have garnered attention and respect globally. Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel announced the award to honor Machhar's bravery. The pilot is currently recovering from his injuries and is receiving well-wishes from across the nation.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Watch: Hero flydubai pilot treated shortly after landing; airlifted to Abu Dhabi.
An alarming incident unfolded on a flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv when co-pilot attacked pilot Smit Machchhar, resulting in a mid-air emergency landing. Machchhar’s quick thinking enabled him to unlock the cockpit door, facilitating crew intervention. Passengers stepped in heroically to restrain the co-pilot. Subsequently, Machchhar was airlifted to a medical facility in Dubai as authorities in Saudi Arabia and the UAE begin investigations into this disturbing incident.
